newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Royale Belge sees full-year 1996 profit jump.
newsitem.headline: Royale Belge sees full-year 1996 profit jump.

text.p: Major Belgian insurance company Royale Belge said on Wednesday it expected full-year 1996 group net profit, excluding the capital gain on the sale of its stake in energy and engineering holding company Tractebel, to exceed 7.0 billion francs.
Royale Belge said on Tuesday it would book a 4.0 billion franc capital gain on the sale of its 4.3 percent Tractebel stake to Belgian holding firm Societe Generale de Belgique.

"Non-recurrent elements excepted, the results for the whole bookyear 1996 should remain in line with the first half-year results and exceed seven billion," Royale Belge board member Dirk Renard told a news briefing.
Royale Belge had a 1995 group net profit of 6.2 billion.
Managing director Jean-Pierre Gerard said it was unlikely that the full four billion capital gain would be booked for full-year profits.
"By the end of the year we could very well have some (negative) exceptional elements," Gerard said.
"We cannot just simply add four to seven billion," he said.

Gerard said the capital gain enabled Royale Belge to put aside provisions to cover the cost -- partly or fully -- of adjusting computer systems to four digits ("the Millenium Bug") in 2000 and the change to the single European currency.
He estimated the cost of the adjustments for Royale Belge's insurance business in Belgium at more than 800 million francs.
The cost of adjustments in its banking business was estimated at 400 to 500 million francs.
